source_cut.review: Visual review across the full running time at five-second intervals, plus selected high-resolution playback and visible editorial notes. Audio was not transcribed. Source share links and raw footage are kept out of this public package.

generator: OpenAI built-in image generation; model identifier not exposed by the tool
measurement_note: Creative packaging concepts, not literal frames or tested CTR winners. Influint Theory entries are design hypotheses and Warning entries are avoided failure modes; no forecast CTR or causal uplift is claimed.

principles.text: Subject and background must differ in colour or the subject becomes unrecognisable at scroll speed — a brown dress on a brown floor, a black jumper behind a black TikTok logo, and a cop's shirt matching the stairs behind him all destroy legibility even though each thumbnail looks fine when studied.

Large channels with busy, cluttered thumbnails (Sidemen, Adin Ross cited) succeed IN SPITE of their packaging, not because of it — their existing fandom supplies the clicks, so their thumbnail style is not a pattern smaller channels should copy.

Thumbnails that look AI-generated cost clicks because viewers perceive them as inauthentic — and on older audiences this has escalated to the point that any photo editing at all triggers accusations of AI and unsubscribes.
A package must be rejected outright when the footage or evidence cannot deliver the result it implies — packaging is a burden of proof, not decoration.

A thumbnail mechanism must be nameable in WORDS before aesthetics are considered, and legible at small size without the title — if only a famous face or copyrighted image carries it, the mechanism does not transfer.

Title and thumbnail must divide labour rather than echo each other — the image carries one half of the promise (result, choice, stakes, specificity) and the title supplies the other half (cause, test, condition, transformation).

A thumbnail should present no more than three (max four) focal elements — text, face, arrow, subject each count as one — because more elements distract from the main image and reduce comprehension at a glance.

Click-through works in two layers, and they are not interchangeable: the package must FIRST be eye-catching, familiar and instantly understood to win attention, and only then deepen into a curiosity gap, novelty or missing information that converts attention into a click. A package that is only mysterious never gets read; one that is only familiar gives no reason to click.

concepts.name: Superman is tiny
concepts.question: Can even Superman beat something this big?
concepts.scene: Extreme scale contrast: the colossal stone-armored, horned Galactus from the footage fills the upper-right two thirds. Tiny recognizable Superman in his blue suit and red cape flies upward toward the giant, clearly separated against an electric-blue rim-lit patch of space. A large natural photographic Alex Stokes in his blue T-shirt occupies the left foreground, pointing toward the absurd scale with focused disbelief. The three anchors form a clean triangle. Keep Superman large enough to recognize; the scale comes from Galactus stretching beyond the frame.

concepts.name: Ender Dragon versus Galactus
concepts.question: Why is Minecraft’s dragon attacking Galactus?
concepts.scene: No human face. Tight opposing diagonals: a clearly block-built black Minecraft Ender Dragon with purple eyes sweeps from the left foreground toward Galactus at right. Galactus is the stone-armored horned giant shown in the reference, his glowing eyes meeting the dragon. Purple dragon particles connect the confrontation without hiding either silhouette. Readable wings, one giant face, simple navy space background. It must look like one playable crossover encounter, not two unrelated posters.

concepts.name: A Banshee under a giant hand
concepts.question: Can the Halo ship get through that gap?
concepts.scene: Ship-level chase camera directly behind a large, instantly recognizable purple Halo Banshee banking through the open gap beneath Galactus’s enormous raised hand. The hand frames the top edge and the giant’s stone-armored face sits beyond it. Pale teal plasma traces lead toward the boss. The Banshee occupies the lower-left third and the enormous hand the upper-right; bright edge separation against a restrained star field. Show a near miss, no invented capture or crushing outcome. No human portrait.

concepts.name: Star Fox meets the final boss
concepts.question: Can this little spaceship stop that giant?
concepts.scene: Cockpit-adjacent cinematic view along the white-and-blue nose and wing of a Star Fox Arwing in the bottom-left foreground. Its clean engine trail curves toward the gigantic armored Galactus in the upper-right distance. One straight burst of laser fire gives the eye a path between ship and boss. Unlike the other space designs, this image feels like the viewer is the pilot: wide perspective, strong foreground wing, one distant enormous face, crisp white ship against dark blue space. No people, no HUD.

concepts.name: Five worlds, one final boss
concepts.question: What happens when all these games fight together?
concepts.scene: A wide, clean boss-battle formation: Galactus’s enormous stone-armored head and torso dominate the right half. A compact V-shaped team at left consists of Superman, a black blocky Ender Dragon, a pale Skyrim-style dragon, a purple Halo Banshee and a white-blue Star Fox Arwing, all aimed at the same boss. Treat the five allies as ONE readable clustered formation with distinct silhouettes and generous space between them, not five equal poster panels. No real human face. Use one coordinated converging attack arc and a simple bright-edged cosmic backdrop.
